text:
Alex Chen: quick sync -- drafting a PRD for unified metering + quota UI/API changes customers asked for. need alignment on scope + launch criteria.
Maria Patel: can you outline the main asks from customers? short list is fine.
Alex Chen: main asks: 1) per-tenant hard+soft limits (reserved for Dedicated) 2) previewed bills for changes to quota/commit 3) clear metering semantics (tokens vs requests) 4) API error/headers for limits + admin UI to change caps.
Samir Gupta: engineering constraints: per-tenant KV cache + quota counters add ~15% latency at tail if we do strict checks on request path. we can async-bill but enforcement needs sync.
Tess Rivera: for UX, customers want an "adjust quota" flow that shows forecasted monthly delta before they confirm. must include model mix & quantization assumptions.
Jordan (finance): pricing semantics question: do we bill by token always, or allow request-based packages (e.g., N calls/month for embeddings)? both requested. we need clear conversion rules.
Zara (legal): for enterprise contracts we need minimum granularity in SOWs for disputes: timestamped metered events + retention window (12 months). also define dispute process for rounding.
Alex Chen: draft acceptance criteria I've put together: - API returns X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (per-tenant + per-model when applicable). - 429 with body explaining soft vs hard breach and billing impact. - Admin UI: adjust cap, preview cost delta, set soft threshold alerts. - Billing exports: CSV/day with token counts by model.
Maria Patel: +1. can you add an edge-case: model fallback when a tenant exceeds quota (auto-fallback to lower-cost variant)? customers want continuity.
Samir Gupta: we can implement fallback policy: route to compatible cheaper variant (same architecture) or degrade to cached responses. caveat: output quality regression must be visible in console. that adds telemetry events.
Alex Chen: here's a sample 429 payload for the API error we propose:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "quota_exceeded",
  "scope": "tenant",
  "limit_type": "soft", // soft: notify + suggest upgrade; hard: block
  "suggested_action": "upgrade_quota or wait_until=168h",
  "retry_after_seconds": 3600
}
```
Samir Gupta: pls note: we should return numeric usage in headers too to make client-side backoff simpler.
Jordan (finance): for pricing rules: propose canonical unit = input_tokens+output_tokens. Support two pricing modes: PAYG (per-token) and COMMIT (monthly reserved tokens at discount). COMMIT contracts should accept overage at a known uplift (e.g., 1.25x). Need wording for prorating when upgrading mid-cycle.
Tess Rivera: UI details: - In quota modal show: current usage %, projected burn for next 30/90 days, projected spend in current pricing mode, and an "estimate if upgraded" toggle. - Also add an audit trail showing who changed quota + reason.
Zara (legal): add requirement: audit trail must be exportable and include signed event IDs for enterprise. retention per customer setting (min 90 days).
Alex Chen: risks/edge cases: - multiple rapid quota changes causing race conditions - clients spoofing headers if we expose them publicly (we need signed headers for admin endpoints) - quantization/packing changing token counts between dev/production -> need canonical tokenizer used by metering pipeline.
Samir Gupta: implementation plan (high level): phase 1: metering pipeline + canonical tokenizer + headers + 429 body (infra + hosted). phase 2: admin UI + preview cost calc + commit contracts integration. phase 3: per-tenant hard limits for Dedicated + fallback routing.
Maria Patel: launch criteria proposal: - Phase 1: unit tests + 99th pct latency impact <5% on text endpoints, billing CSV parity test vs analytics, docs + SDK changes. - Phase 2: usability tested with 3 pilot customers, billing preview matching invoice within 2% for pilot month.
Jordan (finance): also require analytics retention export for audits before GA.
Alex Chen: decisions needed in this thread: 1) canonical pricing unit (tokens only vs allow request packages) 2) overage uplift rate for COMMIT deals 3) soft vs hard default policy and opt-in for fallback routing.
Tess Rivera: leaning toward tokens-only canonical unit (simpler), allow request-packages as syntactic sugar that map to token budgets in contract translation.
Jordan (finance): agree tokens-only internally. expose request-packages as alias that we convert using a well-documented conversion table. need approval from sales on conversion table.
Zara (legal): on overage uplift, suggest capped uplift and explicit notification windows to avoid surprise billing liabilities.
Alex Chen: action items: - Samir: prototype 429 + headers + canonical tokenizer in a branch (ETA 2 weeks) - Maria: draft UI mockups for quota modal + preview (ETA 1 week) - Jordan: propose COMMIT uplift numbers and proration rules (ETA 3 days) - Zara: draft contract clause for metering disputes + audit retention (ETA 4 days)
